div.div: Q. 1 عَرْبَدَ , inf. n. عَرْبَدَةٌ, He showed illnature, or an evil disposition, and behaved unsociably, towards his cup-companion. (TK.) One says, هُوَ يُعَرْبِدُ عَلَى أَصْحَابِهِ عَرْبَدَةَ السَّكْرَانِ He behaves in an annoying manner towards his companions as does the drunken. (A.) Accord. to some, this verb is from عِرْبَدٌّ as signifying “ a red and malignant, or noxious, serpent. ” (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
